policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: The ASV wording does not explicitly distinguish the qere omission from the ketiv אם; no mapped textual-variant note is provided, so both candidates remain compatible and the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV 'I will bring my words' is compatible with both the qere מֵבִיא and ketiv מבי, and the sole mapped note is classified alternative_rendering, so it cannot decide the textual reading; the documented qere base remains the fallback.
